channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Google Lets Schools Turn Off Gemini, But Not the AI in Search
item.description: Schools that want their K-12 students to have access to Google Search will soon have to turn it on themselves, and the AI features built into Search will come with it, under changes the Alphabet Inc. company announced Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Davey Alba

item.title: Some 'Overexuberance' In AI: Sadek Wahba
item.description: Sadek Wahba, founder, chairman and managing partner at I Squared Capital, and author of "Build: Investing in America’s Infrastructure", joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." I Squared Capital closed its second infrastructure credit fund after raising $3 billion, in another sign of surging investor demand to finance the global buildout of power, data centers and other major projects (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Uber President, Longtime Executive Hazelbaker Departs for OpenAI
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. President Jill Hazelbaker is leaving the ride-hailing giant to lead communications at OpenAI, becoming the latest veteran executive to depart Uber this year.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Delivery App Grab Sees Return on AI, Says CFO
item.description: Grab CFO Peter Oey says the company is seeing returns from its use of AI tools in the form of higher spending by customers. The ride-hailing, delivery and financial services app raised its full-year revenue and profit forecasts. Oey joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech" to discuss Grab's earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Disney Plans Thousands of Layoffs Companywide
item.description: Walt Disney is planning thousands of job cuts across the company, including TV, film and parks, with some managers being asked to target 20% in annual cost savings, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Chris Palmeri discusses Disney's plans and how they fit into the changes the wider entertainment industry is experiencing. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple's Upbeat Outlook Overshadowed by Margin Squeeze
item.description: Apple predicted revenue growth of 7% to 10% during the holiday season, but a warning that gross margins would be smaller due to higher memory costs and expenses related to the new Siri AI digital assistant, weighed on the stock. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman discusses how demand for the company's new iPhone Duo and sales of other phones could impact Apple. He speaks with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AllianceBernstein’s Yu Urges Investors to Diversify Beyond AI
item.description: Investors who rode the technology rally this year should look beyond the biggest tech stocks as growing doubts about the artificial intelligence boom rattle markets, says AllianceBernstein’s head of equities Nelson Yu.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Kniazhevich

item.title: European Defense Tech on Autonomous Systems
item.description: Uwe Horstmann, Founder & CEO, STARK and Luciana Lixandru, Partner, Sequoia Capital, discuss how autonomous systems and private capital are reshaping Europe’s defense technology sector with Bloomberg’s Tom Mackenzie at Bloomberg Tech 2026 in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Releases iOS 27.3 Beta With Watch AI Listening Tools, Health App, China AI
item.description: Apple Inc. rolled out the first developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3 on Tuesday, putting new features like always-listening artificial intelligence tools, its AI platform for China and a fresh Health app into widespread testing.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Kelly and Mark Gurman

item.title: AI’s Future Earnings Potential
item.description: How will AI giants like Anthropic and OpenAI pay the bills for vast computer warehouses when they are so far seeing few productivity gains? Bloomberg Opinion columnist Parmy Olson shares the weak justifications she’s been hearing from Silicon Valley execs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Disney Plans Thousands of Layoffs, Targeting 20% Cost Savings
item.description: Walt Disney is moving toward thousands of job cuts with the entertainment giant asking some managers to target 20% in annual cost savings, according to people familiar with the matter. The savings could come from job eliminations as well as from expense reductions, said the people, who asked to not be identified because the discussions are private. Bloomberg's Geetha Ranganathan joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Inference Startup Fal Raises Capital at $16 Billion Valuation
item.description: Fal, an AI inference startup that hosts image, video and audio models for creators and developers, has doubled its valuation to $16 billion in a new round of funding.Bessemer Venture Partners, an existing investor, led a $1.3 billion financing round in the startup in October, Fal is set to announce Tuesday. Other investors include Nvidia Corp., Sound Ventures, HOF Capital and T. Rowe Price Group Inc. Fal previously raised $350 million in a Sequoia-led round in April at an $8 billion valuation.Ta
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas

item.title: Goldman Limits Traders and Bankers From Using Some AI Tools
item.description: Goldman Sachs has annoyed some employees by curbing their access to certain AI tools. Nicole Sy explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s Narrowing Margins Overshadow Upbeat Holiday Forecast
item.description: Apple Inc. delivered a mixed outlook to investors in its first quarterly report under Chief Executive Officer John Ternus, with tightening profit margins overshadowing an upbeat sales forecast. Dan Ives, Partner at Yorkville Ives & Co., discusses the AI buildout and recaps Apple and Palantir earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Can Apple Defend Its Premium?
item.description: Apple’s 36x forward earnings valuation leaves little room for bad news. Craig Moffett, the Founding Partner and Senior Analyst at MoffettNathanson says slowing services growth, rising memory costs and iPhone supply limits are testing the story. He joins Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about why the new foldable is drawing interest and why it won’t solve Apple’s bigger ecosystem and growth questions. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Firm Tied to Some OpenAI, Anthropic AI Hacks Blames ‘Error’
item.description: A spate of cyberattacks involving AI agents from some of the world’s top model makers were down to a human error and time pressures at Israeli security company Irregular Security, according to Chief Executive Officer Dan Lahav.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Robertson and Marissa Newman

item.title: Binance Hackers Used Fake Job Interviews in Record Heist
item.description: Binance Holdings Ltd. said Tuesday that the hackers behind a $6.3 billion heist used social engineering techniques including fake job interviews, as well as malicious software, in the most detailed report yet on how the incident unfolded.
item.dc:creator: Ben Weiss and Ryan Weeks

item.title: Meta Set to Raise $15 Billion in US Leg of Cross-Border Bond
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. is set to raise $15 billion from a US dollar bond sale, drawing solid demand after offering juicier yields to win over buyers in the face of growing skepticism over Big Tech’s massive bet on artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Brian Smith, Davide Barbuscia, Michael Gambale and Ronan Martin

item.title: How AI and Autonomous Aircraft Are Changing Warfare
item.description: Gary Steele, CEO, Shield AI, discusses how AI-piloted aircraft and autonomous drones are changing modern warfare and the balance of military power with Bloomberg’s Tom Giles at Bloomberg Tech 2026 in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Palantir Outlook Signals Slowdown in AI-Fueled Sales Growth
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc., the AI-powered data and analytics platform that counts the US military among its chief customers, issued a quarterly outlook that pointed to a potential slowdown in sales growth.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Martin
